description.value: An fMRI study of how avoidant and anxious adult attachment dimensions modulate neural responses during social emotion perception and regulation in healthy adults.

spans.text: This fMRI study investigated how AAS modulates the perception and regulation of social emotions.

value: AV might be associated with greater use of behavioral suppression (ESUP) and/or reduced re-evaluation (REAP), whereas AX should more strongly involve cognitive up-regulation (REAP) and/or difficulties in the suppression (ESUP) of negative emotions.

AV is also associated with reduced attentional biases to attachment-related emotional information, but these effects are reversed by cognitive load, suggesting an active inhibitory control of attention requiring cognitive effort.

We assessed individual AAS with a validated French version (Guédeney, Fermanian, & Bifulco, Citation 2010 ) of the original Relationships Scales Questionnaire (RSQ; Griffin & Bartholomew, Citation 1994 ).

description.value: The questionnaire assessed adult attachment style, including avoidant and anxious attachment scores.

spans.text: Following recent recommendations (Kurdek, Citation 2002 ), we analyzed the RSQ according to the bi-dimensional model of AAS (Simpson et al., Citation 1992 ), in which scores for attachment (avoidance) (AV) and anxiety (AX) were calculated for each subject by taking into account 13 items (8 for AV and 5 for AX) out of the total 30 items contained in RSQ.
